title: Data Efficiency and Transfer Robustness in Biomedical Image Segmentation: A Study of Redundancy and Forgetting with Cellpose
what_it_is: Cellpose study: a dataset-quantisation (DQ) subset of 10% of the data saturates performance; fine-tuning on a new domain causes forgetting of the source, and replaying a DQ-chosen 5-10% of source data restores it while full replay hurts target adaptation (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: Our few-shot track trains on pool + labelled E1; this says to replay only a small, diverse slice of the 532-cell pool when fine-tuning on a new layout or source, rather than all of it, so recall on the new modules is not diluted while pool scores are kept.
risk_or_reason_against: Evidence is instance segmentation of cells with Cellpose, not thin lines; E1 is now training data, so a new unseen set is needed to measure it.

title: Extending nnU-Net Is All You Need
what_it_is: AMOS-2022 winning entry: nnU-Net with a residual encoder, larger batch and patch, an ensemble of 5 folds x 3 configurations (softmax averaging), and per-class postprocessing (connected components, minimum-size rules with a safety rate) chosen on the cross-validation predictions [full text read].
why_it_could_help_us: The transferable part is the CV-tuned per-class postprocessing: choose a minimum crack-component length and a minimum inactive-region area on our 5-fold out-of-fold predictions. That targets the false-crack-pixels-on-crack-free-cells guard and rare false inactive blobs without retraining.
risk_or_reason_against: 3D CT organs, where size priors are strong; crack fragments are thin and small, so a size cutoff can delete true short cracks and lower recall on E1.

title: Scaling nnU-Net for CBCT Segmentation
what_it_is: ToothFairy2 entry built on nnU-Net ResEnc L: disabling only left/right mirroring raised F-case Dice from 0.7445 to 0.9083, 1500 vs 1000 epochs was a minor gain, a larger patch was best, and per-class small-component cutoffs were tuned on 5-fold CV; MultiTalent pretraining gave no gain after postprocessing [full text read].
why_it_could_help_us: Two lessons map to us. (1) Augmentation symmetry must match the label semantics: check that D4 flips are label-safe for every class (e.g. classes tied to busbar or edge position) before keeping full D4. (2) Per-class, per-metric component cutoffs tuned on out-of-fold predictions are a cheap postprocessing arm.
risk_or_reason_against: The authors note the postprocessed CV numbers are optimistic (cutoffs tuned on the same cases); 3D data.

title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
what_it_is: Controlled study of DINOv2 + LoRA (bias-only up to full fine-tune) against nnU-Net-recipe U-Net and ResU-Net on polyp, breast ultrasound and dermoscopy, with external test sites [full text read].
why_it_could_help_us: Adapted DINOv2 had higher DSC on all 8 external sets (precision-driven in polyp/breast), but within the training distribution a U-Net matched it, and DINOv2 more often missed small lesions entirely and had coarser boundaries (16x16 patch grid at 224 px). This splits our two failure modes: an FM prior may help E1 recall and false positives, while a full-resolution path is needed for 1-2 px cracks. It argues for a hybrid, not a swap.
risk_or_reason_against: Our DINOv3 ConvNeXt-T screen (A8) was KILL; lesions here are blobs, not lines; ViT patch grid is the opposite of what cracks need.

title: LUMOS: Latent Universal Medical Priors for Segmentation
what_it_is: A frozen VFM (DINO, SigLIP) feeds distilled spatial cues ('Pathfinder') into a conventional medical segmentor ('Inspiror'), so the U-Net keeps its own full-resolution path; DINO gave stable matched-backbone gains (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: This is the hybrid the FM-vs-U-Net study points to: keep HRNet/U-Net++ for thin-line precision and inject frozen DINO features as a guidance signal for context (module layout, half-cut edges) aimed at E1 recall. Unlike A8, the VFM does not replace the encoder.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract only; no thin-structure evidence; overlaps in spirit with Dino U-Net (P043) and SAM2-UNet (P002) in MASTER.

title: SA-UNetv2: Rethinking Spatial Attention U-Net for Retinal Vessel Segmentation
what_it_is: 0.26M-parameter U-Net with cross-scale spatial attention in every skip and a 0.5 BCE + 0.5 differentiable MCC loss; all baselines retrained with the same block (DropBlock, GroupNorm) and loss [full text read].
why_it_could_help_us: Thin-vessel 2D data with 20 training images (DRIVE): F1 82.82 vs 81.30 for U-Net and 81.18 for U-Net++ under one recipe, STARE 82.81 vs 79.74. The MCC loss is a cheap new loss for the crack channel (it penalises FP and FN symmetrically, matching relF1), and the skip spatial attention is a small decoder change.
risk_or_reason_against: Gain over its own predecessor SA-UNet is small (+0.38 F1); MCC loss was not ablated against BCE alone; we saw no decoder effect so far.

title: nnU-Net Revisited: A Call for Rigorous Validation in 3D Medical Image Segmentation
what_it_is: ResEnc presets M/L/XL; CNN U-Nets beat transformers and Mamba when confounders are controlled (from D25).
why_it_could_help_us: Already RUN_AFTER_GATE; re-confirmed here as the family anchor; no new 2D thin-structure evidence found.

risk_or_reason_against: Default augmentation not label-safe for 1-2 px lines.

title: Improving Segmentation of Objects with Varying Sizes in Biomedical Images using Instance-wise and Center-of-Instance Segmentation Loss Function (ICI loss)
what_it_is: Two-part loss: an instance-wise term over connected components (so small instances count as much as large ones) plus a center-of-instance term; on ATLAS R2.0 it beat Dice loss by 1.7-3.7% and blob loss by 0.6-5.0% Dice (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: Missed cracks on unseen modules are often whole faint segments; an instance-wise term weights each crack component equally, which targets component recall rather than pixel count. Also applies to the rare inactive regions (42 of 478 cells).
risk_or_reason_against: Same family as CC-DiceCE (P115, RUN_NOW) and blob loss (P326); test only if P115 is positive or as its variant. Crack components may merge into networks, so instances are ill-defined.

title: Cellpose3: one-click image restoration for improved cellular segmentation
what_it_is: Restoration networks (denoise, deblur, upsample) trained so their output is well segmented by a frozen generalist segmenter, plus a perceptual term, over many datasets (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: A segmentation-aware restoration front end, trained across our five sources plus the 11,938 unlabelled cells, could normalise low-contrast sources before the segmenter; aimed at E1 recall where contrast differs.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract only; per-source calibration and intensity normalisation already failed here; a restorer can hallucinate or erase 1-2 px lines.

title: Revisiting Data Augmentation for Ultrasound Images
what_it_is: Benchmark of 14 augmentations, one at a time and in growing top-N sets, on 7 ultrasound segmentation tasks (UltraBench) [full text read].
why_it_could_help_us: Segmentation gains from augmentation were small (best single, brightness, +2.03% on average), effects were task-specific (Gaussian noise +2.77% on one task, -40.41% on another), and adding more augmentations first helps then hurts. Supports screening each augmentation separately for our crack channel instead of adopting nnU-Net's default set.
risk_or_reason_against: Ultrasound, blob-like targets; no thin structures.

title: Why is the Winner the Best?
what_it_is: Survey of all 80 ISBI 2021 / MICCAI 2021 challenges linking method descriptions to rank [full text read].
why_it_could_help_us: Winners used ensembles over seeds, splits and heterogeneous models 5.6x, 1.7x and 2.5x more often, tuned hyperparameters on the challenge metric, and spent twice as much time on failure analysis; in-domain pretraining was rated more important than ImageNet. Supports selecting checkpoints and thresholds on relF1@2 itself and a heterogeneous (HRNet + ResNet) ensemble rather than seed-only.
risk_or_reason_against: Survey; after multiple-testing correction no factor was significant; our same-architecture ensembles (PF2E, SKR2E) already failed.

title: KGS-UNet: KAN-Gated Skip Connections for Small-Structure Medical Image Segmentation with Limited Data
what_it_is: Spline (KAN) gates at each skip connection and a KAN attention downsampling block meant to retain thin structures (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: Benchmarked against over 70 U-Net variants in one framework; top on DRIVE and CHASEDB1 (+1.5% IoU and F1). Small data, thin vessels, which resembles our crack setting.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract only; not open access; KAN layers are slow; we found no decoder effect so far.

title: nnLoGoNet: a hybrid local-global network for retinal vessel segmentation with Skeleton Recall Loss
what_it_is: Parallel CNN + Transformer blocks inside the nnU-Net framework, trained with Skeleton Recall Loss; claims SOTA on OCTA and colour fundus vessel sets (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: 2D thin-vessel model in an nnU-Net trainer; long-range branch could help layout context on unseen modules while the CNN branch keeps detail.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract only; Skeleton Recall already tested here (helped once, failed as ensembles).

title: How to build the best medical image segmentation algorithm using foundation models: a comprehensive empirical study with Segment Anything Model
what_it_is: 18 SAM fine-tuning combinations (ViT-T/B/H; decoder-only vs encoder+decoder; full vs Adapter vs LoRA) on 17 radiology datasets, compared with nnU-Net and U-Net variants [full text read].
why_it_could_help_us: Fine-tuned SAM was only slightly better than nnU-Net; PEFT in both encoder and decoder was best; full fine-tuning of ViT-H collapsed (e.g. about -35% DSC on one MRI set), and the encoder size mattered little. If SAM2-UNet (P002) is run, use LoRA/adapters in the encoder, not a plain fine-tune (matches our finding that the plain fine-tune erased pretrained layers).
risk_or_reason_against: Radiology organs and lesions; ViT patch grid; no thin structures.
